info.desc: Sublime is the third and final album released by the band Sublime, on July 30, 1996, two months after frontman Bradley Nowell's death. The album was a major commercial success, going five times platinum in 1999 and etching Sublime into a permanent place among the stars of mid-90s alternative rock. Its most popular single, "What I Got", was an uncharacteristically poppy song; the bulk of the album was faithful to Sublime's ska, dub, and reggae influences, with tempos ranging from the frantic — such as "Seed," "Same in the End," and "Paddle Out" — to the slow and deliberate, such .

podcast.body: Recorded in late winter and spring of 1996 and intended for release that summer, this self-titled album was considered a "killer record" by those who heard it in advance. Its release became posthumous following singer Brad Nowell's death just after its completion. Multiple albums featuring previously recorded material were released after Nowell's death, with two achieving platinum or gold status, cementing Sublime's status as a "great lost band of the 90s." "They recorded a self-titled album in the late winter and spring of 1996. And those who heard it in advance thought this was going to be a killer record when it was scheduled for release that summer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was a "major label affair" that was anticipated to be a massive success. Despite Brad Nowell's death just six weeks before its scheduled release, it became a "massive hit" and was certified platinum by the end of 1996. "The band had just finished recording their third album and this was a major label affair and the buzz was that it was going to be huge."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This self-titled album was recorded at Willie Nelson's Studio and produced by Paul Leary of the Butthole Surfers. Hopes were very high for this record, which was released shortly after Bradley Nowell's death and propelled Sublime to major success. "Their next album was a self-titled thing made it Willie Nelson Studio and produced by Paul Leary of the Butthole Surfers."
